https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canterbury_Plains

The area was previously forested, now it is a mix of agriculture and intensive livestock. Winds coming from the Southern Alps have their moisture removed as they pass over the mountain range and are hot and dry.

Droughts are common on the plains, especially in the summer. Recent increases in bores into underground aquifers to support intensive dairy farming have lowered the water table by 10m near the surface.

Ground temperature increases by 30-35 degrees C every kilometre, ie boiling point at just 3 km. Aquifers provide a significant cooling effect on the underlying bedrock, vast pressures are involved in this giant seam of steam and rock. Waimakiri river. 20 years ago in the summer flow, It was approx 55 cumecs, and now it is 33 cumecs. Rakaia River, 20 years ago it flowed at 95cu, and now it is down to 65cu.

Intensive drawing of water from the aquifers has affected the lubrication & cooling of the entire plate causing more severe Canterbury earthquakes. Alternately the opposite may be occuring; Where the reduction in water allows remaining water to expand and increases the temperature.
